summary: Both editions were reviewed independently against all five paragraphs of the selected working Greek. No concrete fidelity defect was identified. Both preserve the moral obligation, comparative responsibility, condemnation to death, double punishment, dying forever, exclusion and purification, resulting unity, and concluding request. The simplified edition’s sentence divisions retain these relationships. The notes distinguish editorial restorations and the bracketed speech attribution from preserved text, disclose the stated alternatives, and accurately reflect the supplied bounded reports for the God and loves-to-do-good readings. Acceptance is limited to source fidelity and disclosure within the supplied materials; it does not authenticate unseen manuscripts, certify editions, or establish exhaustive collation. No replacement wording was proposed.
